title: Trying to make AI-assisted 3D space stations feel believable in-game
author: ImaginaryProgram142
selftext:
I've been building an AI-assisted 3D asset pipeline for my unannounced near-future space game. The goal is to create consistent, game-ready assets that let a solo developer tackle a much larger world.

These screenshots are from the current day/night cycle.

Do these stations feel like believable commercial infrastructure in low Earth orbit, or is there anything that breaks the illusion?

comments.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
comments.body: I think I would expect harsher lighting

comments.author: argefox
comments.body:
Are you going for realistic, sci-fi looks, futuristic, retro futuristic? 

There's a ton to unpack for space building and your style defines the constrains.

replies.author: ImaginaryProgram142
replies.body: I'm aiming for near-future orbital infrastructure. Modular stations inspired by the ISS, fuel depots, shipyards, and industrial facilities. The overall vibe is sci-fi with subtle cyberpunk influences.

replies.author: argefox
replies.body:
Well, that narrows it down but the scope is... broad enough to be almost anything.
I'd concept it out with modular containers, bulky square stuff, you can slap the cyberpunk/modern/retro skins on the outside, depending on how many pipes and brass gears are visible =P

comments.author: Nervous_Teach_5596
comments.body: The night should be an actual night (search NASA pictures, I think their pictures are even free to use?) also the solar panels (the 8 in 2 pair) position are a pretty bad placed, bc the light is from top to down, and the earth is beyond the satellite, so light should be in that position, and panels also, and on a place that gets shadow, (what to do when it rotate is up to you and also the "earth rotation", maybe also rotate the solar panels to the sun light when they're facing to the earth?)

replies.author: ImaginaryProgram142
replies.body: No release date yet! I'm still building it out and trying to do things the right way instead of rushing. I'll keep posting updates because I like talking about the game almost as much as I enjoy making it. Thanks for the feedback.

comments.author: PleasantCitron1685
comments.body: Blue out the planet a little; atmosphere is thick, especially at angles. Also makes everything above the planet more visible.

comments.author: Aureon
comments.body:
are those 2d or 3d?   

on a backdrop, you really cannot use 2d stylized assets. You will need 3d models with perfect light-angle matching.

replies.author: ImaginaryProgram142
replies.body: Yep, all 3D models. I've been iterating on the lighting recently, and your comment made me take another look at the light direction relative to Earth. I also found a material issue that wasn't helping. Thanks for the feedback!
